about: Lists of values in code (`list<integer>`, `list<text>`, `list<decimal>`, `list<bool>`) and random, as every runtime gives them. `xs[i]` reads or sets item i, counted from 1. A position outside the list fails with exactly `there is no item <i> in a list of <n>`. `random(max)` in an engine written in Clarity gives a whole number from 1 to max: 1 + (the next number of splitmix64 as an unsigned 64-bit number, modulo max). `random` cases start the sequence from `seed` and list what the calls give in order. A max below 1 fails with exactly `random takes a highest number of 1 or more, not <max>`.

items.fails: there is no item 0 in a list of 3
there is no item 4 in a list of 3
there is no item 1 in a list of 0
there is no item -1 in a list of 3

random.fails: random takes a highest number of 1 or more, not 0
